newsitem.title: FRANCE: Truckers block French roads in tax protest.
newsitem.headline: Truckers block French roads in tax protest.

text.p: Truckers blocked several key access roads into the French capital and to towns in southwest and central France on Thursday in a protest over fuel taxes.

Hundreds of lorry drivers used their vehicles to blockade several roads into eastern Paris and tie up the Paris ring road, but authorities said traffic holdups were no worse than usual for a rainy Paris morning.
They said many suburban commuters who had been forewarned left early for work or took alternative routes.
Truckers also set up blockades in the southwestern Dordogne and central Haute-Vienne departments, obstructing roads to several towns including Perigueux, Sarlat, Bergerac and Limoges.
The National Road Transport Federation (FNTR) and the National Union of Road Transporter Associations (UNOSTRA) had organised the protest to press their demand for lower taxes on diesel fuel.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe pledged in a letter to union leaders and made public on Thursday that future diesel tax increases would not exceed the rate of inflation.

"In 1997, the rise in duties will be reduced by more than half compared to 1996, and brought to a level comparable to the rate of inflation," Juppe wrote in the letter released by the prime minister's office.
"The government will continue this policy, and increases in duties over the years to follow will not exceeed the rate of inflation," he said.
Juppe also promised to defend truckers' interests in any talks with its European Union partners on petrol duties.

The two unions, which represent drivers from about half of France's 35,000 road transport firms, argue that taxes on diesel fuel are lower for other workers including taxi drivers, fishermen and farmers.

A truckers' group in the Dordogne said the department's 200 road transport firms employing 2,500 people would show no profit in 1996 because of rising pay costs, payroll charges and increases in tolls and diesel prices.
